tasks.title: Language layer as data: extension map and four node-type tables

details.goal: Make language support a table lookup so adding a language is a data edit, never a code path.
details.contract: types.ts exports type LangId (the 12 MVP ids: python, typescript, tsx, javascript, go, java, rust, c, cpp, csharp, php, ruby), interface LangSpec { id, extensions: string[], grammarWasm: string, classTypes: string[], functionTypes: string[], importTypes: string[], callTypes: string[], testFileRegex?: RegExp }, and the resolved row type. registry.ts exports EXTENSION_MAP (ext to LangId, deterministic order, includes .py .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .cjs .go .java .rs .c .h .cpp .cc .hpp .cs .php .rb), LANGS (LangId to LangSpec), detectLanguage(path): LangId | null, and specFor(id). The four node-type lists are the node-versus-edge decision expressed as data: classTypes produce class nodes, functionTypes produce function nodes, importTypes and callTypes produce edges. Include a header comment stating that name/grammar values were validated against the vendored grammar node-types, and one test that every LangId in LANGS has at least one function and one call type.
steps: Write types.ts with LangId, LangSpec and the row type
Write registry.ts with EXTENSION_MAP for the 12 languages
Fill the four node-type lists per language from the grammar node-types, copying the patterns CRG uses (for example python class_definition, function_definition, import_statement, call)
Implement detectLanguage and specFor
Add tests/lang.test.ts asserting every language has function and call types and that .h maps to c while .cpp maps to cpp
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/lang.test.ts. Done when all 12 languages satisfy the type-list assertions and detectLanguage resolves every extension in EXTENSION_MAP to its declared language.

tasks.title: WASM parser pool with a bounded per-language LRU

details.goal: One parser entry point that loads a grammar on demand, bounds memory, and returns a tree plus any parse-error ranges.
details.contract: parse.ts exports initParsers(): Promise<void> (initialises the web-tree-sitter runtime once per process), parseFile(path, source, lang): Promise<{tree, errorRanges: string[]}> and disposeLang(lang). Grammars load from tree-sitter-wasms in node_modules by the grammarWasm name in the LangSpec; a missing grammar resolves to an error with reason grammar_unavailable, never a throw out of parseFile. Parser instances are cached in an LRU of max 6 languages keyed by LangId, each with a reset() before reuse. errorRanges is computed by walking the tree for ERROR and MISSING nodes and formatting as comma-separated 1-based line ranges with a cap of 20 ranges plus a count suffix. No file may be parsed twice concurrently in this module. Package versions are @modelcontextprotocol/sdk independent: web-tree-sitter 0.27.2, tree-sitter-wasms 0.1.13 as installed by TASK-001.
steps: Write initParsers using web-tree-sitter Parser.init()
Implement the language LRU with reset-before-reuse
Implement parseFile mapping LangSpec.grammarWasm to the wasm file and returning errorRanges
Handle an unavailable grammar as a structured result rather than an exception
Write tests/parse.test.ts parsing one Python and one TypeScript snippet and asserting errorRanges is empty
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/parse.test.ts. Done when both snippets parse with zero error ranges, and a request for a fabricated grammar returns reason grammar_unavailable without throwing.

tasks.title: Repository discovery with exclusions and coverage reasons

details.goal: Walk a repository deterministically and record both what is indexed and what is skipped, with a reason.
details.contract: discover.ts exports discover(repoRoot, {ignorePatterns?}): Promise<{files: Array<{path, lang, size, sha256}>, notIndexed: Array<{path, reason, language?}>, skipped: number}>. Rules: always exclude .git, node_modules, .codegraph, dist, vendor; honour repoRoot/.gitignore and repoRoot/.codegraphignore with simple glob matching; skip files larger than 512 MiB with reason size_cap; skip binary files (NUL byte in the first 8192 bytes) with reason binary; record a file whose extension is unknown as reason unsupported_ext; compute sha256 for every accepted file. Paths are repo-relative with forward slashes and no leading dot-slash. Deterministic ordering by path so two runs produce identical output.
steps: Implement the recursive walk with the always-exclude list
Add .gitignore and .codegraphignore parsing with glob matching
Add the binary, size and unsupported-extension classifications with reasons
Compute sha256 for accepted files and sort by path
Write tests/discover.test.ts over a temp tree containing one .ts file, one binary, one unknown extension and one ignored path
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/discover.test.ts. Done when the fixture yields exactly one indexed file and three notIndexed entries with reasons ignored, binary and unsupported_ext, in deterministic order.

tasks.title: Generic table-driven extractor for nodes, containment and raw edges

details.goal: One cursor walk driven by the four node-type lists that produces nodes plus unresolved call and import targets.
details.contract: extract.ts exports extractFile(tree, spec, relPath): {nodes: ExtractedNode[], rawEdges: ExtractedEdge[], unresolved: UnresolvedSite[]}. ExtractedNode carries kind (file|module|class|function|method|test|endpoint), name, qn built as relPath::Scope.name, startLine, endLine, signature, isTest, props (decorators, modifiers as JSON). Walk rules: a node matching classTypes emits a class node and pushes it onto the scope stack; functionTypes inside a class emit method nodes, outside emit function nodes; a node matching callTypes emits a rawEdge with target = the callee text and tier extracted_candidate; importTypes emit rawEdges with target = the imported module text; anything inside a call or import that cannot be named goes to unresolved with evidence_kind dynamic. Containment edges are emitted as contains from the enclosing file or class node to every declared node. The file node is always emitted first. No language-specific if branches other than a documented exception table with at most 3 entries.
steps: Write the scope stack and the file and module node emission
Implement classTypes and functionTypes handling with method versus function distinction
Implement callTypes and importTypes producing rawEdges
Collect unresolved sites with evidence kinds
Emit contains edges for every declared node
Write tests/extract.test.ts over a Python fixture asserting node kinds, qns and at least one containment edge
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/extract.test.ts. Done when the Python fixture yields a file node, a class node, method nodes with the path::Class.method qn form, one containment edge per declaration and no unresolved entry.

tasks.title: Binding pass: resolve raw edges by same-file, import and inheritance evidence

details.goal: Turn raw edge targets into resolved node ids where evidence exists, and leave the rest in unresolved with a reason.
details.contract: resolve.ts exports bind(units: FileUnit[], index: SymbolIndex): {edges: ResolvedEdge[], unresolved: UnresolvedSite[]}. FileUnit is the per-file extractor output. SymbolIndex maps qn and bare name to node ids and records imports per file. Binding order for a raw call or import target: exact qn within the same file, then a name visible through that file's imports, then a unique name in the whole index when exactly one node matches, then a superclass method when the receiver's class inherits it, otherwise unresolved with evidence_kind one of receiver_type_unknown, ambiguous (more than one candidate) or dynamic. Every resolved edge carries tier extracted for same-file and import evidence and tier inferred for unique-name and inheritance evidence. Never emit an edge whose target id does not exist.
steps: Define SymbolIndex construction from units including per-file import tables
Implement the four-step binding order
Assign tier per evidence kind
Route every failure to unresolved with the matching evidence_kind
Write tests/resolve.test.ts covering a same-file call, an imported call, an ambiguous name and an unknown receiver
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/resolve.test.ts. Done when the four cases produce respectively resolved extracted, resolved extracted, unresolved ambiguous and unresolved receiver_type_unknown, and no edge is emitted with a missing target.

tasks.title: Persist a generation: metrics, FTS delta, tombstones

details.goal: Write one indexed unit set into the stage database and make the derived data consistent in the same transaction.
details.contract: persist.ts exports persistUnit(tx, unit, resolved): void writing nodes, edges, unresolved and not_indexed for one file after deleting that file's previous rows by file_id; and finalizeGeneration(tx, {generationId, baseCommit, mode}): {nodes, edges, tombstones} which recomputes node_metrics for touched nodes plus their two-hop neighbourhood (in_degree, out_degree, is_entry, tested_depth as min hops to a test node, reachable_count only on full publish), updates node_fts_state and the node_fts index by rowid delta, appends a tombstone row for every qn that disappeared since the previous generation, and inserts the generation row plus meta.generation. FTS delta falls back to a full rebuild when the delta exceeds 35 percent of node rows. All writes go through the open transaction; no function in this file opens a connection.
steps: Implement persistUnit with file-scoped delete then insert
Implement degree and tested_depth recomputation for the touched neighbourhood
Implement the FTS delta with the 35 percent rebuild threshold
Implement tombstone append for disappeared qns
Insert the generation row and update meta.generation
Write tests/persist.test.ts asserting a second persist of an edited file replaces rows and leaves one tombstone
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/persist.test.ts. Done when re-persisting an edited fixture deletes the removed symbol, records exactly one tombstone, keeps node counts consistent and leaves node_fts matching the node names.

tasks.title: Index worker entry: lock, incremental routing, publish, exit codes

details.goal: A standalone process that owns the writer and reports one machine-readable result, so the MCP server never indexes in-process.
details.contract: worker.ts exports runWorker(opts: {repoRoot, dataDir, force, mode}): Promise<number> returning 0 published, 2 nothing to do, 75 lock held, 1 failure. Sequence: acquireLock (index_locked returns 75), ensure data dir and .codegraph/.gitignore containing a single star, migrate, discover, compute changed files by comparing sha256 against the file table and by git diff against meta generation base_commit, if nothing changed and not force return 2, withStage: persist each changed unit, bind edges, finalizeGeneration, seal, publish. On any throw: discard the stage, bump meta.consecutive_failures, set meta.indexer_state to failed, return 1. On success set indexer_state to idle. stdout must stay empty; all reporting is on stderr or the exit code. This file is invoked by bin/codegraph.ts worker mode and by the watcher; tools must never import it.
steps: Implement option parsing and the lock acquisition with the 75 exit code
Implement data dir setup including the single-star .gitignore
Implement the incremental changed-file computation
Implement the withStage orchestration calling persistUnit and finalizeGeneration
Implement success and failure metadata writes and exit codes
Write tests/worker.test.ts running runWorker on a temp repo twice, expecting 0 then 2
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/worker.test.ts. Done when the first run returns 0 with one generation row, the second returns 2, and stdout captured during both runs is empty.

tasks.title: Phase 1 closing gate: parser parity and full-corpus index

details.goal: Prove the indexer meets the four parser acceptance criteria and produces a real generation from the reference corpus.
details.contract: parser-parity.test.ts indexes code-review-graph/ read-only into a temp data dir, then asserts: every one of the 12 languages files parse without rising ERROR count above 1 percent of files; per-language node counts are within 5 percent of the CRG oracle recorded in TOOL-OUTPUTS.md for python and typescript, and non-zero for the other languages present; p50 parse time at most 4 ms per file and p95 at most 25 ms per file, measured over at least 200 files. index-integration.test.ts runs runWorker on the same corpus and asserts: one generation row, node and edge counts printed to progress, unresolved rows exist and are non-zero, not_indexed contains no entry whose reason is unsupported_ext for a language we claim to support, and a second run returns 2 (idempotent). Both tests must leave code-review-graph/ unmodified (assert git status --porcelain on it is empty).
steps: Write tests/parser-parity.test.ts with the three parser assertions and timing measurement
Write tests/index-integration.test.ts with the generation, unresolved and idempotence assertions
Run both against code-review-graph/ and record the measured numbers
Assert the reference corpus is unmodified after both runs
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/parser-parity.test.ts tests/index-integration.test.ts. Done when all assertions pass and the recorded p95 parse time and per-language node counts are written into the progress log as evidence.
